answers.label: Organization type, other specified
answers.text: We are acedmic but representing the professional service industry group.

answers.label: Feedback on clarified MBM definition
answers.text: Disagree with hourly matching & deliverability – would slow global decarbonization and restrict impactful procurement.

answers.label: Comments on opposition to QC4
answers.text: No support for mandatory hourly matching. Using load profiles would be very difficult for professional services firms. In general, our load is small because electricity is used solely in commercial office space for routine office activities; in addition, offices are relatively small and spread across a large global footprint, and there would be little or no instances of two offices in the same market grid location. Limited accuracy, high cost, discourages global participation.

answers.label: Comments on opposition to QC5
answers.text: No support for mandatory deliverability requirements. In general, our electricity use is small and often global. Renewable energy adoption and climate change transcends grid borders. Broader market boundaries offer advantages, such as enabling procurement from regions with lower renewable generation costs. This requirement may result in de-investment on renewable energy.

answers.label: Why that US boundary upholds deliverability
answers.text: Other - National. A single market approach for the US and Canada is preferred, as outlined in the RE100 Technical Criteria. Narrow boundaries reduce flexibility and impact; should remain optional. Broader market boundaries offer advantages, such as enabling procurement from regions with lower renewable generation costs.

answers.label: Comments on support for exemptions
answers.text: Electricity load profiles vary greatly by industry and company size. Allowing exemptions to lower-emitting companies, like professional services, reduces the reporting burden and allows companies to invest in pragmatic solutions.

answers.label: Comments on chosen eligibility option
answers.text: Option 3 addresses both companies in lower-emitting industries (e.g. professional services) AND smaller companies. This reduces the reporting burden on these entities with limited impact through their scope 2 emissions and allows them to invest in impact elsewhere in their footprints.

answers.label: Reasons for supporting the legacy clause
Comments on support for legacy clause
answers.text: Corporate buyers should not be penalized for contracts signed under the current standard, as their purpose is to advance clean energy and reduce Scope 2 emissions. Legacy treatment should match the term of PPAs, long-term EACs, or green tariffs, since these agreements are essential for developers and utilities to secure financing and regulatory approvals.
